$comment: nana-pi's own map, generated by the generator this repo ships (scripts/code-map.mjs is a shim over templates/typescript/template/scripts/code-map.mjs). Two layers: the apps and the repo's own scripts on top, the packages under them — within a layer imports are free, and nothing in a package may import an app. One 'packages' entry with an empty prefix because nana-pi publishes as ONE package (`pi install git:` installs the whole repo), so a relative import between its directories — packages/nana-knowledge/lib -> packages/nana-pack/lib/display.mjs, apps/desk -> packages/nana-stage/lib/sign.mjs — crosses no published boundary. The six test roots are mapped too, each declared layerExempt: a test module is a module (the 'every module' contract has to reach the suite, or a dropped test header fails nothing), and a test may import across the layer direction. They are declared as roots in their own right so the exemption applies — apps/desk/test and apps/bench/test also sit under the apps/desk and apps/bench roots, which is harmless duplication. 'ignore' names what sits under a root but is outside the map: the three paths that exist only as text INSIDE a test (`apps/bench/test/src.mjs`, `apps/bench/lib/blocks.mjs`, `packages/nana-pack/ts-probe.ts` are fixture sources a test writes at runtime and quotes an import of, which the regex scanner cannot tell from a real edge), the recorded study trees, the browser-only e2e suites, the fixture trees, and templates/ (shipped template SOURCE, whose contract headers name the RENDERED project's paths, not this repo's — so the shims' import of the generator is an external edge). Exemptions are the three bench modules content-pinned by a closed study's fingerprint (apps/bench/studies/tool-profiles-2026-09-08/study.json pinnedSha) — a header would alter committed evidence.

layers.title: Apps and scripts
layers.blurb: The desk, the bench and this repo's own scripts — the entry points. They may import the packages; a package may not import them.

layers.title: Packages
layers.blurb: The pi extension pack, the knowledge pull, the staged-block layer and the setup bootstrap — the installable units. Within the layer imports are free (nana-pi ships as one package); nothing here may reach up into an app.
